items.q: Statement 1: 'Cheaper overseas resources would discourage reshoring for a low-cost business.' Statement 2: 'Political instability overseas would discourage reshoring.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 true: if overseas resources are cheaper and you're pursuing a low-cost strategy, you'd want to stay overseas (not reshore). Cheap overseas resources discourage bringing production home. Statement 2 false: political instability overseas would encourage reshoring (bringing production home for safety), not discourage it. Reshoring = bringing production back to the UK. Instability abroad makes you want to come home.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Outsourcing a business function can allow a firm to benefit from the specialist expertise of an external provider while reducing its own fixed costs.
Statement 2: A major risk of outsourcing is that the business may lose direct control over the quality and reliability of that function.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are correct. Outsourcing converts fixed internal costs to variable external costs and brings in specialist skills. However, the firm is now dependent on a third party and cannot directly supervise standards, so quality and reliability can suffer — a commonly tested downside of outsourcing.
items.label: New question

items.q: Efficiency ratios for 4 companies. Payables days, Receivables days, Inventory turnover. Which has BEST cash flow?
opts: Company A (35 payables, 25 receivables, 15 turnover)
Company B (35 payables, 25 receivables, 10 turnover)
Company C (25 payables, 35 receivables, 15 turnover)
Company D (25 payables, 35 receivables, 10 turnover)
items.why: Best cash flow = high payables days (delay paying suppliers) + low receivables days (collect from customers quickly) + high inventory turnover (sell stock quickly). Company A: 35 payables (high), 25 receivables (low), 15 inventory turnover (high) - the best combination. Think about cash flow: you want money IN fast (low receivables), money out slow (high payables), and stock sold quickly (high inventory turnover).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Globalisation has generally increased the degree of competition faced by domestic firms in developed economies.
Statement 2: An emerging economy is best defined as one that has completed its industrialisation and achieved a high GDP per capita.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Globalisation opens domestic markets to foreign competitors, so Statement 1 is true. An emerging economy is one that is experiencing rapid growth and industrialisation but has not yet reached the income levels of developed economies — Statement 2's definition describes a developed economy, making it false. Students frequently conflate emerging and developed economies.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'A business might improve quality to make demand more price inelastic.' Statement 2: 'A business might improve quality to achieve a competitive advantage.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both true. Higher quality creates brand loyalty and differentiation, making consumers less price-sensitive (more inelastic) and providing competitive advantage. These are two well-established benefits of quality improvement.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A bank overdraft is:
opts: An external source of long-term finance
An external source of short-term finance
An internal source of long-term finance
An internal source of short-term finance
items.why: A bank overdraft comes from an external source (the bank) and is short-term finance (repayable on demand, used for day-to-day cash flow management). Overdrafts are external (from a bank) and short-term (not for long-term investment).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A government imposes a tariff on imported steel. Which of the following is the most likely immediate effect on a domestic car manufacturer that uses imported steel?
opts: Its revenue will increase because consumers will switch to domestically produced cars.
Its production costs will rise, potentially reducing its price competitiveness.
It will benefit because the tariff protects it from foreign car manufacturers.
Its profit margin will widen as the tariff reduces the supply of competing imports.
items.why: A tariff on an input raises the cost of that input for all users, including domestic manufacturers. The car manufacturer's costs increase, squeezing margins or forcing price rises. Option C confuses the tariff on steel (an input) with a tariff on finished cars. The tariff does not directly protect the car manufacturer from foreign car competition.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table 1 shows four scenarios of changes in interest rates and wages. Which scenario is most likely to encourage a business to change from labour-intensive processes to capital-intensive processes? A: Interest rates increase, Wages increase B: Interest rates increase, Wages decrease C: Interest rates decrease, Wages increase D: Interest rates decrease, Wages decrease
opts: Scenario A
Scenario B
Scenario C
Scenario D
items.why: Scenario C: Decrease in interest rates + Increase in wages. Lower interest rates make borrowing for machinery cheaper. Higher wages make labour more expensive. Both push towards capital-intensive production. Students often pick A (both increase) but higher interest rates make capital more expensive to finance. You need cheaper capital and more expensive labour.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which action would improve a manufacturer's ability to RESPOND to changes in consumer demand?
opts: Ensuring workers are highly trained in one specialised role
Maintaining high capacity utilisation levels
Outsourcing more production to other manufacturers
Reducing warehouse size to minimise inventory
items.why: Outsourcing gives flexibility - the business can scale production up or down by adjusting contracts with external manufacturers, without being constrained by its own fixed capacity. Option A reduces flexibility (workers can only do one thing). B leaves no spare capacity for demand changes.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Intrapreneurship always requires a separate business unit to be established within the organisation.
Statement 2: A key advantage of intrapreneurship over external entrepreneurship is that the intrapreneur can draw on the resources of the existing firm.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Intrapreneurship is entrepreneurial activity within an existing organisation; it does not require a separate unit — it can occur within existing teams. The genuine advantage is access to the parent firm's capital, expertise and infrastructure, making Statement 2 true. Students often confuse intrapreneurship with spin-off structures, so wrongly accept Statement 1.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Sole traders are usually private sector organisations.' Statement 2: 'Public limited companies are usually public sector organisations.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true - sole traders are private sector. Statement 2 is false - PLCs are private sector. 'Public' means shares are publicly traded, not government-owned. One of the most common A-Level mistakes. 'Public limited company' does not mean public sector.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A patent grants its holder the exclusive right to use an invention commercially, typically for 20 years from the date of application.
Statement 2: Once a patent is granted, the holder is not required to disclose the details of the invention to the public.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A patent does give exclusive commercial rights for typically 20 years, so Statement 1 is true. However, disclosure is a condition of the patent system — the inventor must publish the invention in exchange for the monopoly right, making Statement 2 false. Students often believe patents keep inventions secret; in fact, secrecy is the alternative strategy (trade secrets).
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Lean production reduces unit costs by buying raw materials in greater bulk.' Statement 2: 'Lean production reduces unit costs by reducing wastage of raw materials.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false - lean production uses JIT which means buying smaller, more frequent deliveries, not bulk buying. Statement 2 is true - reducing waste (muda) is the core principle of lean production. Lean = JIT = small frequent deliveries, not bulk buying. Bulk buying is the opposite of lean inventory management.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Strategy X: positive YED goods. Strategy Y: economies of scope. Statement 1: 'X fails if GDP declines.' Statement 2: 'Y needs wider product range.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both true. Positive YED + falling GDP = falling demand = Strategy X fails. Economies of scope require product variety. Positive YED means demand moves with income. GDP decline = income decline = demand decline.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: After five years of trading, a company's initial ordinary share capital is identical to its market capitalisation. No further shares have been issued. These two values will only be identical if:
opts: All of its profit has been distributed to shareholders
All of its profit has been retained in the business
It has made a total profit of zero over the five years
The current market price of the shares is the same as the initial share price
items.why: Market capitalisation = shares x current price. Initial share capital = shares x original price. Same number of shares means these are only equal if the current price equals the original price. Students often pick C (zero profit), but profit doesn't directly determine share price in this simple way. Focus on the mathematical relationship.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Brenton Foods is a UK snack manufacturer considering entering the Indian market. It plans to use the same product recipe and packaging as in the UK. Which term best describes this approach, and what is its principal risk?
opts: Localisation; the risk is that adapting the recipe and packaging for every regional sub-market significantly increases production complexity and unit costs compared with a uniform approach.
Standardisation; the risk is that the product may not match local tastes or cultural preferences.
Diversification; the risk is that entering an unrelated overseas market exposes the firm to unfamiliar competitive dynamics and regulatory environments it has no prior experience navigating.

Glocalisation; the risk is that making superficial adaptations to packaging while retaining the original recipe fails to satisfy local consumers and simultaneously dilutes the firm's established brand identity.
items.why: Selling an unchanged product globally is standardisation. Its main risk in a diverse market like India is a mismatch with local consumer preferences, dietary norms or regulatory requirements. Option D describes glocalisation (adapting a global product locally), which is the opposite of what Brenton is doing. Option A also describes the opposite strategy.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Consider the following statements about strategic drift.

Statement 1: Strategic drift occurs when an organisation's strategy gradually falls out of alignment with its changing external environment.
Statement 2: Strategic drift is most likely to occur in organisations that frequently and radically change their strategy in response to environmental shifts.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is the standard definition of strategic drift — small incremental adjustments that do not keep pace with environmental change. Statement 2 is false and describes the opposite situation; strategic drift is associated with organisations that are too slow and cautious in changing strategy, not those that change too frequently.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Comparative advantage provides a reason for international trade even when one country is absolutely more efficient at producing all goods.
Statement 2: Economies of scale provide a demand-side reason for a business to sell in overseas markets.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Comparative advantage shows that mutually beneficial trade is possible even when one party has an absolute advantage in everything, so Statement 1 is true. Economies of scale are a supply-side benefit of accessing larger markets (higher output lowers unit costs); they are not a demand-side reason, making Statement 2 false. Students often mix up supply-side and demand-side drivers of international trade.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following is the best example of overlapping stakeholder interests?
opts: Employees want higher wages, which raises unit labour costs; shareholders want those costs minimised to protect dividend payments and share price
A supplier wants prompt payment to maintain its own cash flow; the business wants to delay payment as long as possible to protect its own working capital position
Customers want lower prices to maximise their own value; competitors want the business to charge higher prices so that rivals can undercut it and gain market share
Employees want job security; customers want consistent product quality from a stable workforce
items.why: Overlapping interests occur where two stakeholder groups both benefit from the same business outcome. A stable, secure workforce tends to produce consistent quality, so employees' desire for job security aligns with customers' desire for reliable products. Options A, B, and C all describe conflicts rather than areas of overlap.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a trademark from copyright?
opts: A trademark protects original literary and artistic works for the life of the creator plus 70 years, whereas copyright protects brand names and logos used in trade.
A trademark must be registered to offer legal protection; copyright arises automatically on creation of an original work.
Copyright lasts indefinitely provided renewal fees are paid every ten years, whereas a trademark expires automatically after 70 years regardless of use.
Both trademark and copyright require formal registration with the Intellectual Property Office and payment of a fee before they can be legally enforced against infringement.
items.why: In the UK, copyright arises automatically when an original work is created and requires no registration, whereas a trademark must be registered to gain statutory protection. Options A reverses the definitions. Option C confuses trademark renewal (which does require periodic renewal fees) with copyright duration (life of author plus 70 years). Option D is incorrect because copyright needs no registration.
items.label: New question
